gaps.sentence: The author, about ___ there has been much debate, will speak at the festival.
gaps.hint: debate about the author — person after preposition
gaps.explanation: 'About whom' is required after the preposition 'about' when referring to a person.

gaps.sentence: The scientist ___ research we cited has won the Nobel Prize.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose' shows possession: the scientist whose research…

gaps.sentence: It was the first time ___ I had ever driven on my own.
gaps.hint: after 'the first time', use this pronoun
gaps.explanation: 'The first time that ...' is the standard pattern; the pronoun may also be omitted, but 'which' and 'what' do not fit.

gaps.sentence: Have you got anything ___ will remove this stain?
gaps.explanation: After 'anything', 'that' is the preferred relative pronoun; 'which' is avoided after -thing words.

gaps.sentence: The assistant ___ I spoke to was extremely helpful.
gaps.explanation: 'Whom' is the formal object form after a preposition-style clause.

gaps.sentence: The 1990s was the decade ___ mobile phones became common.
gaps.explanation: 'When' replaces 'in which' after time nouns; 'which' cannot stand alone here.

gaps.sentence: I will always remember the summer ___ we cycled along the Danube.
gaps.explanation: 'When' relates to a time expression like 'the summer'.

gaps.sentence: The committee rejected a plan ___ costs had been underestimated.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose costs' means 'the plan's costs'; 'which' would need 'the costs of which'.
